questions.question: A manager states that a perimeter firewall makes further security measures unnecessary. Which principle does this view ignore?

options.A: Separation of duties: firewall rules must always be written and approved by exactly the same person
options.B: Fail-safe defaults: firewalls are only allowed to deny traffic that has been listed explicitly in advance
options.C: Least privilege: firewalls can only be operated by users who have administrator rights on all systems
options.D: Defense in depth: multiple layers of controls are needed because any single control can fail

questions.explanation: A firewall is one control. Attackers can bypass it through phishing, insiders or web application flaws, so additional layers such as hardening, monitoring and application-level controls are needed.

questions.question: A server has a critical unpatched vulnerability but is reachable only from a small, monitored management network. How does this context affect the risk assessment?

options.A: The risk is eliminated completely, since a vulnerability can only be exploited from the internet by anonymous users
options.B: The lower exposure reduces the likelihood, so the risk may be lower than for an internet-facing server, but it is not zero
options.C: The risk is higher than for internet-facing servers, since management networks are attacked more often by criminals
options.D: The vulnerability no longer exists, because vulnerabilities are defined by the network zone that they are placed in

questions.explanation: Risk combines likelihood and impact. Limited reachability lowers the likelihood of exploitation, but insiders, compromised hosts or later network changes can still make the flaw exploitable.

questions.question: A vulnerability is announced in a library used by the application, and no patch is available yet. Which response is most appropriate?

options.A: Remove the library from the vendor's website so that the flaw cannot be found by anyone else in the meantime
options.B: Find where the library is used, add compensating controls and monitoring, and patch when available
options.C: Publish the internal exploit details, so that the community can create a patch in the shortest possible time
options.D: Wait silently for the patch and take no action, since nothing can be done about a flaw without an official fix

questions.explanation: Without a patch, risk can still be reduced by knowing your exposure and adding mitigations and monitoring. Inaction or publishing exploit details increases risk.

questions.question: Encrypting every field and every internal message would slow the system and complicate operations. Which approach reflects a sound security testing and design view?

options.A: Apply protection in proportion to the sensitivity of the data and the risks, and verify that the chosen controls work
options.B: Encrypt everything using the weakest algorithm available so the performance impact is as small as possible
options.C: Never encrypt anything, since performance is always more important than protection of data
options.D: Encrypt only the data that is unimportant, since important data can be protected by good passwords

questions.explanation: Security controls have costs, so they should match risk. Testing then checks that the controls chosen for sensitive data are correctly implemented and effective.

questions.question: An attacker gains a foothold via a phishing email, uses stolen credentials to reach other machines, and finally obtains administrator rights. What does this scenario imply for security testing?

options.A: Each weakness must be tested completely independently, since combinations never change the resulting risk
options.B: Attacks are often multi-step chains, so tests should consider combinations of weaknesses and not only isolated findings
options.C: Only the phishing email needs testing, since later steps cannot happen without it and are therefore irrelevant
options.D: Privilege escalation never occurs after initial access, so it does not have to be considered in test planning

questions.explanation: Real attackers chain low and medium weaknesses into serious compromises. Tests and risk ratings should take into account how findings can be combined.

questions.question: A password policy requires very complex passwords changed every 30 days, and users start to write passwords on sticky notes. What does this illustrate?

options.A: Complex passwords cannot be guessed, so the notes on the desks cannot create any additional risk
options.B: Users are never the cause of security problems, so the policy must be tightened even further
options.C: Security controls that ignore usability can lead users to bypass them, creating new weaknesses
options.D: Passwords written on notes are always more secure than passwords that are memorized by the users

questions.explanation: Controls must work with human behavior. Overly burdensome rules encourage workarounds, so testing and policy design should consider usability as well as strength.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A new payment feature and an internal wiki are both due for release, and the security test budget is limited. How should the effort be allocated?

options.A: Split the effort equally, so that no system is favored over any other in the organization
options.B: Give the payment feature more testing, because a compromise would have a much higher impact
options.C: Test only the wiki, because it is easier and therefore produces more findings per hour
options.D: Skip testing for both, since limited budgets make security testing pointless

questions.explanation: Risk-based prioritization directs limited effort to the assets where impact and likelihood are highest, which here is the payment feature.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A company passes a compliance audit for a security standard but has not performed technical security testing. What is the most accurate conclusion?

options.A: Technical testing is forbidden by security standards and would cause the company to lose its certification
options.B: The audit results replace the need for any risk assessment in the organization
options.C: Compliance shows that required controls are documented and present, but it does not prove they resist real attacks
options.D: The company is fully protected, because standards require every vulnerability to be removed

questions.explanation: Standards define minimum requirements and controls, and audits check conformity. Technical tests are needed to find implementation weaknesses that an audit does not exercise.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: The security policy requires all data to be encrypted, but a legacy system stores some data in plain text. How should a policy-based test strategy treat this?

options.A: Report the deviation, assess the risk, and agree remediation or a documented exception
options.B: Delete the plain text data from the system so that no deviation can be measured
options.C: Ignore it, since a legacy system does not have to follow the policy of the organization
options.D: Change the policy immediately so that the system counts as compliant without further action

questions.explanation: Policy-based testing compares reality with policy. Deviations become findings, and the owner decides on remediation or accepts the risk through a formal exception.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: During a test, an in-scope server reveals credentials that would allow access to a system that is outside the agreed scope. What should the tester do?

options.A: Post the credentials in the public forum so that the owner is warned as quickly as possible
options.B: Use the credentials to test the out-of-scope system, since the discovery proves that it is connected
options.C: Stop, report the discovery to the contact named in the agreement, and not use the credentials without new authorization
options.D: Delete the credentials from the server so that nobody else can use them afterwards

questions.explanation: Scope limits authorization. Testers report such discoveries and ask for a scope extension, rather than acting on their own or altering evidence.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Management asks whether to run a bug bounty program instead of commissioning a penetration test. Which statement is most balanced?

options.A: Neither is useful, since attackers never find vulnerabilities that the developers have not found
options.B: A bug bounty always replaces penetration testing, since the number of participants is larger
options.C: They complement each other: a bounty gives broad, continuous exploration, while a pen test offers structured, scoped coverage and reporting
options.D: A penetration test always replaces a bug bounty, since paid testers are always more capable than outside researchers

questions.explanation: Bounties bring diversity and continuity but variable coverage, whereas a commissioned test follows an agreed scope and method. Many organizations use both.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A provider of a software-as-a-service product supplies an independent attestation report but does not allow customers to run their own attack tests. What is a sensible strategy for the customer?

options.A: Review the attestation and test the integration and configuration that the customer controls
options.B: Ignore the attestation and attack the provider's systems anyway to verify the claims independently
options.C: Refuse to use any service whose provider does not allow testing by customers
options.D: Accept the attestation as proof that the customer's own configuration is also secure

questions.explanation: Shared responsibility means the customer tests what it controls, such as settings, access management and integration, and relies on evidence for the provider's part.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A data protection officer objects to copying production customer data into the test environment for security testing. Which is the best way forward?

options.A: Use the production system itself for testing, since it already contains the data
options.B: Copy the data anyway, because testers are bound to confidentiality by their employment contracts
options.C: Use masked or synthetic data that reproduces the required characteristics, and protect any remaining sensitive data
options.D: Cancel all security testing until production data may be used without restriction

questions.explanation: Privacy rules limit use of real personal data. Realistic but masked or synthetic data allows testing without exposing individuals.

questions.question: The rules of engagement for a penetration test are being written for a production system. Which element is most important to include for safety?

options.A: A promise that the test will never find any vulnerability that could damage the reputation of the company
options.B: A statement that the testers may change any configuration they like, to prove impact
options.C: Emergency contacts and a procedure for stopping the test immediately if service is affected
options.D: A list of all employee passwords, to speed up the test

questions.explanation: Testing production carries risk of disruption, so both sides need agreed contacts and a quick way to halt activity. Passwords or unlimited changes are not appropriate.

questions.question: To test authorization, the team needs accounts with different privilege levels. Which preparation is best?

options.A: Use the accounts of real employees without telling them, to make the tests more realistic
options.B: Create dedicated test accounts for each role, with documented permissions, and use them to build a role and function test matrix
options.C: Test with no accounts at all, since authorization only matters for anonymous visitors
options.D: Use the administrator account for every test, since it can access everything and therefore covers all roles

questions.explanation: Testing authorization requires identities at each level so that permitted and forbidden actions can be checked. Using administrators or real people's accounts is ineffective or improper.

questions.question: During a scan of a production system, a service becomes unresponsive. What should the tester do first?

options.A: Delete the scan logs, so that the incident is not associated with the testing team
options.B: Continue the scan to finish on schedule, since the outage is only temporary
options.C: Restart the service silently and hope that nobody notices any problem
options.D: Stop the activity, notify the agreed contact, and record what was done and when

questions.explanation: Safety comes first. Stopping, informing the stakeholders and keeping accurate records lets the owner restore service and supports later analysis.

questions.question: A vulnerability scanner will be run against a live system used by customers. Which configuration approach reduces risk?

options.A: Run the scanner from a computer that is not connected to the network
options.B: Agree a time window, use non-destructive checks first, and avoid tests known to crash services unless approved
options.C: Disable all logging on the target system so that the scanner runs without any interruption
options.D: Enable every available check at full speed during business hours to obtain the fastest results

questions.explanation: Scan intensity and checks can affect availability. Windows, gentle settings and explicit approval for risky tests limit harm to production.

questions.question: While testing, the team finds a file containing customer personal data on a server. How should it be handled?

options.A: Publish samples in the report so that the seriousness of the finding is clear
options.B: Limit access, report the finding without copying the data, and protect evidence
options.C: Email the file to the customer's management as proof of the finding
options.D: Download the whole file to the tester's laptop, and share it with the rest of the team

questions.explanation: Testers must minimize their handling of sensitive data. Describing the exposure and protecting evidence avoids creating additional privacy breaches.

questions.question: After the fix of a serious injection flaw, the team must decide the scope of the retest. Which scope is most appropriate?

options.A: No retest, since the developers have confirmed the fix in a message
options.B: The whole application, in exactly the same depth as during the first test
options.C: The original issue, variants of it in similar functions, and areas that the fix may have affected
options.D: Only the exact request that was reported originally, as the fix is only for that request

questions.explanation: Fixes are often incomplete or affect other code. Retesting the original vector, related patterns and the neighborhood of the change gives assurance in proportion to risk.

questions.question: Test results may be needed as evidence in a later legal or disciplinary matter. What should the test process ensure?

options.A: That evidence is stored on a shared drive where everybody can edit it
options.B: That evidence is destroyed immediately after the testing has finished
options.C: That evidence is timestamped, protected from alteration and its handling logged
options.D: That evidence is kept only in the memory of the tester who found the issue

questions.explanation: Evidence needs integrity and traceability so that its origin and handling can be demonstrated. Memory, open editing or immediate destruction undermine its value.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: A requirement states that the system must be secure. How should a security tester respond?

options.A: Reject the whole project, because requirements of this kind can never be tested
options.B: Ask for specific, verifiable requirements, such as authentication, lockout and data protection criteria
options.C: Wait until after release to find out what the requirement was intended to mean
options.D: Accept the requirement as it is, and write a single test that checks whether the system feels secure

questions.explanation: Vague requirements cannot be verified. Refining them into measurable statements enables design, implementation and testing to address security consistently.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: In a data flow diagram, which elements are most important for security test design?

options.A: The names of the developers who drew the diagram, since they know the design best
options.B: The colors used for the different components, since they show the risk level of each component
options.C: Trust boundaries and the points where data crosses them, since validation and authentication are needed there
options.D: The order in which the diagram was created, since it tells which component is most important

questions.explanation: Attacks typically exploit assumptions at boundaries. Focusing tests on data crossing trust boundaries covers the places where controls are most needed.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: In a two-week sprint, the security tester is asked to complete a full penetration test of everything built. Which adaptation is most effective?

options.A: Test increments continuously with abuse stories and automated checks, with deeper tests at milestones
options.B: Skip security testing in sprints, and expect the developers to be aware of every possible attack
options.C: Perform all security testing after the final sprint, since agile teams do not test security earlier
options.D: Extend the sprints to six months, so that a full penetration test fits into each of them

questions.explanation: Agile security testing is incremental: small, frequent checks embedded in the sprint, plus periodic deeper assessments, rather than one big test at the end.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: The CI pipeline fails builds for every scanner finding, including low-severity ones, and developers begin to disable the scanner. What is a better approach?

options.A: Let developers decide individually whether the scanner runs on their own builds
options.B: Turn off the scanner permanently and rely on the annual penetration test only
options.C: Set thresholds based on severity, tune rules to reduce noise, and handle lower findings through a backlog
options.D: Keep failing every build on all findings and require developers to fix everything at once

questions.explanation: Gates must be credible. Severity thresholds and tuning keep the signal useful, while a backlog tracks the remaining issues without blocking all delivery.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: A secret key was accidentally committed to the source repository and later removed in a new commit. Is the key safe?

options.A: No, it remains in the history, so it must be treated as compromised and replaced
options.B: Yes, since deleted files can never be retrieved from a version control history
options.C: Yes, because keys are harmless when they are not used for the next hour
options.D: Yes, as long as the repository is not accessed by more than ten users

questions.explanation: Version control keeps old content. The key must be rotated, and secret scanning should prevent similar commits in future.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: A minor configuration change to a payment service is planned, and the team wants to skip security review because it is minor. What is the appropriate practice?

options.A: Delay the change for a year to plan a full penetration test first
options.B: Apply the change and hope that any problems are detected by the users
options.C: Do a lightweight security impact analysis and retest the affected controls
options.D: Skip any review, since small changes can never affect security

questions.explanation: Small changes can open big holes, such as widening permissions. A risk-scaled analysis and targeted retest keep change agile without ignoring security.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: An application is being decommissioned. Which security activity should be included?

options.A: Keeping the credentials active so that support staff can still connect
options.B: Leaving the system running with its data and accounts in case it is needed someday
options.C: Secure data disposal, revocation of credentials and access, and removal from exposure
options.D: Deleting only the user interface, and keeping the database accessible to everyone

questions.explanation: Retired systems can leak data or provide entry points. Proper disposal and removal of access closes these risks.

questions.question: Firewall rules between network zones include several "any to any allow" entries. How can a tester verify the impact?

options.A: Test connectivity across zones, for example by scanning from the DMZ, and compare with the design
options.B: Ask the users whether the network feels fast enough for them
options.C: Delete all firewall rules, and observe which network services stop working
options.D: Read the rule descriptions only, and accept them as being correct without any further verification

questions.explanation: Actual reachability shows whether segmentation works. Testing across zones confirms or refutes what the rule base and design documents claim.

questions.question: An intrusion detection system generates so many alerts that analysts ignore them. Which test-related action helps?

options.A: Increase the number of rules until every event creates an alert
options.B: Disable the intrusion detection system, because alerts are always a nuisance
options.C: Forward all alerts automatically to the mailbox of the chief executive
options.D: Simulate known attacks to check detection, and tune rules to cut false positives

questions.explanation: Useful detection needs both sensitivity and precision. Simulated attacks show whether important events trigger alerts, and tuning restores analysts' attention.

questions.question: A hardening review of a new server finds default vendor accounts still enabled. How should this be treated?

options.A: As a benefit, because support staff can log in more easily in an emergency
options.B: As a vulnerability: disable or change them, and check the baseline on other servers
options.C: As acceptable, because default accounts have documentation that describes them
options.D: As irrelevant, because attackers do not know default account names

questions.explanation: Default credentials are widely known and often exploited. The finding also suggests that the build process needs to enforce a secure baseline.

questions.question: A multi-factor authentication feature allows a user to reset their second factor by answering security questions. What is the security testing concern?

options.A: The second factor is irrelevant if the first factor is a long password
options.B: Fallback paths are never used, so they do not need to be tested
options.C: The fallback path may be weaker and let an attacker bypass the second factor
options.D: Security questions are stronger than hardware tokens and must therefore be preferred

questions.explanation: Attackers target the weakest route. Recovery and reset flows must be tested to ensure they do not undermine the stronger authentication.

questions.question: A web application places the session identifier in the URL. What risk does this create?

options.A: Nothing, because URLs are never stored or shared by browsers and servers
options.B: The identifier can leak through history, logs or referrers, enabling hijacking
options.C: The session ends automatically, whenever the URL is copied by the user
options.D: The URL becomes shorter, which makes the application faster and less risky

questions.explanation: URLs are recorded in many places and shared through links. Session tokens should be kept in cookies or headers with appropriate protections instead.

questions.question: A tester is asked to create an authorization test matrix for an application with three roles and twenty functions. What does it help to show?

options.A: Which users have the longest passwords among all of the accounts
options.B: Which role may and may not perform each function
options.C: Which developers wrote each of the twenty functions
options.D: Which functions are used most often by customers each day

questions.explanation: A matrix of roles and functions makes expected permissions explicit so that both allowed and denied actions can be tested systematically, which finds missing access checks.

questions.question: Encrypted database files are stored on a server, and the decryption key is stored in a configuration file in the same directory. What is the weakness?

options.A: The weakness is that the files are encrypted, which makes them slower to read
options.B: Whoever obtains the files probably gets the key too, so protection is weak
options.C: There is no weakness, since files and keys should always be stored together
options.D: The weakness is the size of the key, which should always be as short as possible

questions.explanation: Key protection is essential. Separating keys from data, or using a key management service, ensures that theft of the data alone does not expose it.

questions.question: A TLS configuration test shows that an old protocol version and weak cipher suites are still accepted. Which conclusion is correct?

options.A: Attackers may downgrade or break the connection, so the configuration should disable weak protocols and ciphers
options.B: Accepting more options is always more secure, since clients can choose the one that they like
options.C: The weak options only matter if the server is located in another country
options.D: The configuration has no effect on security as long as a valid certificate is installed

questions.explanation: Support for weak options allows downgrade and cryptographic attacks. Hardened configurations accept only strong, current protocols and ciphers.

questions.question: A file upload feature is protected by an antivirus scan. How can the tester check that it works?

options.A: Upload the harmless EICAR test file, also inside archives, to check detection
options.B: Ask the vendor whether the product is good, and accept the answer without testing
options.C: Upload real, destructive malware to the production system to see what will happen
options.D: Upload a photograph and conclude that all malware would be detected as well

questions.explanation: The EICAR string allows safe verification of detection, and testing with different formats reveals gaps such as unscanned archives. Real malware is unnecessary and dangerous.

questions.question: A login form returns "unknown user" for a wrong username and "wrong password" for a wrong password. What is the security concern?

options.A: It improves security, since users can always see exactly what they did wrong
options.B: It has no effect on security because usernames are always public knowledge
options.C: It allows account enumeration, since attackers can discover which usernames exist
options.D: It reveals the password of the user, which is a violation of the policy

questions.explanation: Different responses let attackers build lists of valid accounts for targeted attacks. Generic messages, and similar response timing, reduce this leak.

questions.question: A user's access token remains valid after the administrator has revoked the user's account. What should be tested and expected?

options.A: That the token becomes invalid only when the user closes the browser
options.B: That revoked accounts and tokens are rejected promptly by server checks or short lifetimes
options.C: That revocation only matters for users who have never logged in
options.D: That tokens should remain valid for as long as possible, whatever happens to the account

questions.explanation: Timely revocation limits the window in which a compromised or terminated account can be used. Servers need to check status or use short-lived tokens.

questions.question: A test from the demilitarized zone shows that a web server can connect directly to the internal database server on its management port. What does this indicate?

options.A: A problem only for the database vendor, which has to fix the port
options.B: An improvement, since more connections make the network more resilient
options.C: A correct design, because web servers always need administrative access to databases
options.D: A segmentation weakness that lets a compromised web server reach internal systems

questions.explanation: Zones should restrict traffic to what is necessary. Management access from the DMZ to internal systems enlarges the impact of a web server compromise.

questions.question: A phishing simulation identifies the employees who clicked the link. Which handling is most constructive?

options.A: Use aggregate results to target training, and avoid naming or punishing individuals
options.B: Keep the results secret and never do anything about them
options.C: Dismiss the employees who clicked, to set an example for the others
options.D: Publish the names of everyone who clicked to embarrass them into improvement

questions.explanation: Simulations aim to improve behavior. Blame discourages reporting and harms the culture, whereas aggregated data and support raise resilience.

questions.question: A phone-based social engineering test (vishing) is planned. Which precondition is essential?

options.A: Permission from the employees that will be called, given before the calls are made
options.B: No authorization is needed, since the calls are made to the tester's own colleagues
options.C: A list of personal private phone numbers of the employees, taken from social media
options.D: Written authorization, a defined scope, and awareness of legal and ethical limits

questions.explanation: Social engineering tests involve real people and may raise legal and privacy issues, so management authorization and clear boundaries are essential. Individual consent would defeat the test.

questions.question: Which measure of awareness effectiveness is more informative than the click rate alone?

options.A: The number of training slides created by the security team
options.B: The total number of emails sent by the simulation tool
options.C: The rate of reported suspicious messages, along with click rates
options.D: The number of employees who attended the training in person

questions.explanation: Reporting shows active engagement and helps detect real campaigns early. Attendance or output measures do not show that behavior changed.

questions.question: A tester tailgates into a secured office by following an employee, and the employee holds the door. What is the best follow-up?

options.A: Ignore the result, because physical security is not part of security testing
options.B: Report it, fix the process and awareness, and consider turnstiles or door alarms
options.C: Repeat the test until nobody holds the door, then delete the earlier results
options.D: Blame the employee publicly and demand that they be dismissed immediately

questions.explanation: Physical access controls are part of overall security. Combining awareness, clear procedures and technical controls addresses the underlying weakness without blame.

questions.question: A former employee's account was still active three months after they left and was used to access data. Which process is the weakness?

options.A: Offboarding, where access revocation was not completed and verified
options.B: Network speed, which was too slow for the account to be disabled
options.C: Onboarding, where a new employee was given too many training courses
options.D: Password complexity, which was set too high for the former employee

questions.explanation: Timely removal of access when people leave is a core control. Testing the offboarding process shows whether accounts and privileges are actually revoked.

questions.question: A vulnerability has a high CVSS score but affects an isolated test system with no sensitive data, while a medium-score flaw affects the payment system. How should the report prioritize them?

options.A: Remove the payment system flaw from the report, since it has the lower score
options.B: Always rank strictly by base score, ignoring where the vulnerabilities are located
options.C: Always rank by the age of the vulnerability, oldest first
options.D: Adjust priority using business context, so the payment flaw may rank higher

questions.explanation: Base scores measure technical severity in general. Environmental and business factors such as exposure and asset value determine real priority.

questions.question: A report will be read by executives, developers and auditors. What is the best structure?

options.A: Only raw tool output, since it is complete and objective
options.B: A single technical section that all readers must read in full
options.C: Executive summary, developer findings, and scope and method for auditors
options.D: Only a summary without any details, since details are of interest to nobody

questions.explanation: Different readers need different levels of detail. Structuring the report by audience keeps it usable and defensible.

questions.question: Management proposes ranking development teams by the number of vulnerabilities found in their code. What is the main risk of this metric?

options.A: The metric guarantees that the most secure code is written by all teams
options.B: The ranking will be ignored because nobody reads any security metric
options.C: Teams will always fix every vulnerability faster in response to the ranking
options.D: Teams may hide problems, resist testing, or argue about counting

questions.explanation: Metrics used punitively encourage gaming and reduce openness. Measures should support improvement, for example by tracking trends and remediation time.

questions.question: A test report states "the system has no vulnerabilities". Which wording is more appropriate?

options.A: "No vulnerabilities were found within the agreed scope, time and methods"
options.B: "The system is impossible to attack for any attacker in the world"
options.C: "The testers are certain that nothing could ever be found by anyone else"
options.D: "The system is secure now and will stay secure in the future"

questions.explanation: Testing samples reality and cannot prove absence of flaws. Statements should reflect scope and limits, so that stakeholders do not gain false assurance.

questions.question: Developers dispute a finding as theoretical. Which response best resolves the disagreement?

options.A: Escalate immediately to the chief executive without further evidence
options.B: Remove the finding, so that the developers are satisfied
options.C: Provide a proof of concept or clear reproduction steps showing the impact
options.D: Insist that the finding is right because the tester is more experienced

questions.explanation: Evidence resolves disputes. A safe proof of concept shows exploitability and impact, and helps prioritize the fix.

questions.question: A fix for a serious finding cannot be delivered for three months. What should the report or follow-up record?

options.A: That the testers accept the risk on behalf of the organization
options.B: Nothing, because a finding that is not fixed is not worth documenting
options.C: That the finding is closed, since a fix is planned
options.D: Compensating controls, residual risk, the risk owner, and a review date

questions.explanation: Deferred fixes need visible interim mitigations and an owner's decision, with a review date so that the risk does not get forgotten.

questions.question: Attackers modify a build tool used by many developers, so that every compiled application contains a hidden backdoor. Which security property is primarily violated?

options.A: Availability, because the developers can no longer connect to the internet at all
options.B: Integrity, because the software delivered is not what the developers intended to build
options.C: Confidentiality only, because no data was changed in the build process at any point
options.D: Non-repudiation, because the developers refuse to sign the software that was produced

questions.explanation: Tampering with tools alters the product without the authors' knowledge, which is an integrity failure with wide consequences. It illustrates why the build chain itself needs protection and testing.

questions.question: An employee with legitimate access copies a customer database to a personal drive before resigning. Which controls would address this risk?

options.A: Antivirus software on all workstations, since copying data is a form of malware
options.B: A stronger firewall on the perimeter, since the employee is outside the network
options.C: Least privilege, monitoring of unusual access, and controls that flag large transfers
options.D: Stricter password complexity, since the employee needed a password to log in

questions.explanation: Insiders use authorized access, so perimeter controls are ineffective. Limiting rights, watching for anomalies and restricting exfiltration paths are the relevant measures.

questions.question: A server room has unused USB ports and no access log. An attacker who gets into the room briefly could plug in a device. Which term describes this weakness?

options.A: Network vector, where the attack always travels over the internet
options.B: Physical attack vector: direct hardware access bypasses logical controls
options.C: Cryptographic vector, where the attack relies on weak keys
options.D: Social vector, where the attack is done by telephone

questions.explanation: Physical access can defeat software controls. Testing should therefore consider physical security measures such as locks, logging and disabling of unused ports.

questions.question: Users are directed to a fake copy of their bank's website because their DNS responses were manipulated. Which attribute of security is most directly undermined?

options.A: Portability of the banking application across different browsers
options.B: Availability of electricity in the data center of the bank
options.C: Maintainability of the source code of the website
options.D: Authenticity and integrity of the information that the users receive

questions.explanation: DNS poisoning causes clients to trust a false destination. Defenses such as DNSSEC and certificate validation help ensure that users reach the genuine service.

questions.question: In a risk analysis, which element is best described as the vulnerability?

options.A: Unvalidated input in a web form that permits command injection
options.B: The loss of trust that would follow a publicized breach
options.C: A criminal group that wants to steal customer data
options.D: The customer database that holds valuable information

questions.explanation: A vulnerability is a weakness that can be exploited. The criminal group is a threat actor, the database is an asset, and the loss of trust is an impact.

questions.question: Attackers encrypt a company's data and also threaten to publish a copy that they stole. Which attributes are affected?

options.A: Only integrity, since the data files were changed in any case
options.B: Availability through the encryption, and confidentiality through the stolen copy
options.C: Only availability, since publication of stolen data does not affect confidentiality
options.D: None, because the company still owns the original data files

questions.explanation: Double extortion combines loss of access with the threat of disclosure. Risk assessments and tests should consider both attributes, and backups protect only against the first.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A product is released weekly. The company performs one penetration test per year. Which strategy better matches the release pace?

options.A: Keep only the annual test, because deeper tests are always better than frequent ones
options.B: Combine pipeline security checks and targeted change testing with periodic deep assessments
options.C: Stop testing security between the annual tests, because the system is unchanged in that time
options.D: Perform a full penetration test before every weekly release, regardless of cost

questions.explanation: Frequent change needs frequent feedback. Continuous, risk-focused checks catch new weaknesses quickly, while periodic in-depth testing addresses complex issues.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A penetration test lasted two weeks and found few issues. How should stakeholders interpret this?

options.A: As evidence that the testers were incompetent and should be replaced
options.B: As a reason to stop all further security activities for the next year
options.C: As proof that the system cannot be attacked by any other person
options.D: As a result limited by scope, time and skills, unlike real attackers

questions.explanation: Time-boxed tests sample the attack surface. Few findings raise confidence but do not guarantee the absence of vulnerabilities.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A mobile banking app consists of the app, an API and back-end services. Which test strategy is most appropriate?

options.A: Test all three: client controls and storage, API authentication, and the back end
options.B: Test only the visible screens of the app, since the back end is not visible to users
options.C: Test only the store listing, since it is the entry point for downloads
options.D: Test only the back-end servers, since attackers cannot access the app

questions.explanation: Attackers can target each layer, and the client cannot be trusted. A complete strategy covers the app, its communication and the services behind it.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: Two business units disagree on how much residual risk is acceptable. Which approach helps the test strategy?

options.A: Apply the lowest level of testing to both units to save money
options.B: Test one unit thoroughly, and ignore the other completely
options.C: Ignore the differences, and let testers decide what is acceptable
options.D: Clarify each unit's risk appetite and tailor depth and acceptance criteria

questions.explanation: Risk appetite is a business decision that shapes how much testing is enough. Making it explicit avoids arbitrary depth and disputed exit criteria.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A connected device in the field cannot easily receive software updates. How does this affect the security test strategy?

options.A: Testing is unnecessary, since the manufacturer will fix flaws in the next product
options.B: Testing can be lighter, since devices that cannot be updated are unlikely to be attacked
options.C: Testing should concentrate on the color of the device only
options.D: Testing must be more thorough before release, including firmware and update mechanisms

questions.explanation: When patching is hard, weaknesses live long. Pre-release testing, secure update design and hardening are therefore especially important.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A security lead must justify the testing budget. Which argument is most persuasive?

options.A: Testing will make it impossible for any security incident to occur
options.B: Testing reduces the likelihood and impact of losses from business risks
options.C: Testing gives the team something useful to do between projects
options.D: Testing is required simply because many other companies do it as well

questions.explanation: Investment is convincing when linked to business risk and value. Guarantees or imitation are neither accurate nor persuasive.

questions.domain: Security Testing Purposes, Goals, and Strategies
questions.question: A team wants to rely exclusively on the developers' own security tests for a critical release. What is the main limitation?

options.A: Developers' tests are illegal, since they have not been approved by the government
options.B: Developers always find more vulnerabilities than independent testers do
options.C: Developers cannot write tests, since tests can only be written by testers
options.D: Lack of independence: authors may share the blind spots and assumptions that caused the weaknesses

questions.explanation: Developer tests are valuable but a fresh view often finds what authors miss. Critical releases benefit from independent assessment as well.

questions.question: A team must estimate effort for testing a large application. Which input is most useful?

options.A: The number of interfaces, roles and functions in scope
options.B: The total number of employees who work in the whole company
options.C: The number of vacations that the testers took last year
options.D: The length of the mission statement on the company website

questions.explanation: Effort scales with the size of the attack surface and the depth of testing. Unrelated numbers do not help estimation.

questions.question: An authenticated scan keeps logging itself out, because it follows the logout link and misses most pages. What is the appropriate fix?

options.A: Turn off authentication and scan only public pages, ignoring the rest of the site
options.B: Remove the logout link from the site permanently for all users
options.C: Accept the low coverage and report the site as fully tested
options.D: Exclude the logout function, maintain the session, and check the crawl coverage

questions.explanation: Scanner configuration determines coverage. Excluding destructive or session-ending functions and verifying what was crawled produces meaningful results.

questions.question: A tester performs exploratory penetration testing. How can coverage be managed?

options.A: Follow a fixed script without any deviation, whatever is discovered
options.B: Do not plan anything, and record nothing, since exploration cannot be documented
options.C: Use charters with defined objectives and time boxes, and record areas explored and findings
options.D: Test only areas that the tester finds interesting, and skip the others

questions.explanation: Charters focus exploration and produce traceable records, so that management can see what was examined even without scripted tests.

questions.question: While testing, a tester finds a critical, easily exploitable flaw on an internet-facing system. When should the tester report it?

options.A: Only in the final report, weeks later, to keep the report complete
options.B: Never, since the flaw is outside the tester's responsibility
options.C: Only when the owner asks whether any flaws have been found
options.D: Immediately to the agreed contact, without waiting for the final report

questions.explanation: Serious exposure justifies immediate escalation so the owner can act, according to the agreement. Waiting leaves the system open to real attackers.

questions.question: The test environment lacks the web application firewall that is present in production. How should results be interpreted?

options.A: Assume production is safe, since a firewall exists there in any case
options.B: Assume production behaves identically, since the environments are the same in every respect
options.C: Discard the results completely, because environments must be identical to be useful
options.D: Note the difference, since a WAF may hide flaws, and validate in an equivalent setting

questions.explanation: Differences between environments affect what tests show. A WAF may mask flaws that remain exploitable, so the gap should be documented and addressed.

questions.question: A test window collides with a company freeze period for a critical business event. What should the team do?

options.A: Cancel the entire security testing program permanently
options.B: Reschedule or agree a reduced-risk approach with the owner
options.C: Proceed as planned, since tests have priority over business events
options.D: Test secretly at night, so nobody notices the activity

questions.explanation: Testing must fit operational reality. Agreeing changes with the owner avoids unintended disruption and maintains trust.

questions.question: A scanner finds nothing, but a manual test finds an authorization flaw. What does this illustrate?

options.A: The scanner is the only trustworthy source, so the manual finding must be wrong
options.B: Tools miss logic and access control flaws, so techniques should be combined
options.C: Authorization flaws cannot exist in applications that have been scanned
options.D: Manual testing is never useful, since tools find everything that exists

questions.explanation: Tools find patterns but struggle with context-dependent flaws. Combining techniques improves coverage.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: In a microservice architecture, services call each other with tokens. What should security testing of this design include?

options.A: Whether each service validates tokens and permissions itself
options.B: Only the speed of communication between the services
options.C: Only the names of the services in the source code
options.D: Only the front-end service, since internal services cannot be attacked

questions.explanation: Internal trust is a common weakness. Each service should authenticate and authorize requests so that a single compromise does not spread freely.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: A static scan of infrastructure-as-code templates finds a security group open to the entire internet on a database port. How should this be handled?

options.A: Deploy it anyway and review the configuration at the end of the year
options.B: Treat it as a defect, restrict the access, and add a pipeline check
options.C: Ignore the finding, since templates are not real systems
options.D: Delete the scanner that reported the issue

questions.explanation: Misconfigurations are cheaper to fix before they are deployed. Pipeline checks stop the same mistake from recurring.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: A team applies dependency updates automatically. Which practice keeps this safe?

options.A: Block all updates permanently, to avoid the risk of change
options.B: Apply updates only once every five years, in a single large batch
options.C: Apply all updates without any test, since updates are always safe
options.D: Run automated tests, including security checks, on each update

questions.explanation: Updates fix vulnerabilities but can also introduce problems. Automated verification allows quick, frequent updates with confidence.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Which type of weakness is a security-focused code review more likely to find than automated tools?

options.A: Files with the wrong extension in a repository
options.B: Spelling mistakes in the comments
options.C: Logic flaws such as missing authorization checks
options.D: Known vulnerable library versions listed in a database

questions.explanation: Reviewers understand intent and context, so they can spot flawed logic. Tools are better at finding known patterns and library versions.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: A late pre-release penetration test finds a serious architectural flaw, and a fix would delay the launch by months. What lesson applies?

options.A: Architecture never has security flaws, so the test result must be wrong
options.B: Penetration tests should be postponed even later to avoid such surprises
options.C: Threat modelling and design review should begin earlier, when changes are cheaper
options.D: Security testing should be dropped, as it only causes delays

questions.explanation: Design flaws are costly to change late. Earlier reviews and testing reduce the risk and cost of last-minute findings.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: Operations receive many security alerts, but nobody knows whether critical events would be noticed. How can this be tested?

options.A: Assume that alerts always work as soon as monitoring software is installed
options.B: Run simulated attacks and check that alerts fire and are handled
options.C: Increase the volume of alerts so that some will be noticed
options.D: Disable all alerts, and see whether anyone complains

questions.explanation: Detection and response depend on tools, rules and people. Exercises prove whether the entire chain works.

questions.domain: Security Testing Throughout the Software Lifecycle
questions.question: The architecture changes by adding a third-party payment provider. What should happen to the threat model?

options.A: Nothing, since threat models never change after they are first created
options.B: Update it with the new interface, data flows and trust boundaries
options.C: It should be deleted, because the provider takes over all security responsibility
options.D: It should be kept secret from the provider and from the developers

questions.explanation: New integrations create new attack paths and dependencies. Keeping the model current keeps testing aligned with actual risk.

questions.question: A tester examines a company's wireless network. Which finding is most concerning?

options.A: A guest network with access to the internal network
options.B: A guest network with a different name from the corporate network
options.C: A network name that contains the name of the company
options.D: A network that is available in the meeting rooms

questions.explanation: Missing separation lets guests or attackers on the wireless network reach internal systems. Network segregation and strong encryption are basic controls.

questions.question: An application writes user-supplied text into its log file without any handling, and an attacker submits text containing line breaks and fake entries. What is this weakness?

options.A: Cross-site scripting, which only affects the browsers of users
options.B: A denial of service, which stops the logging from starting
options.C: Session fixation, which sets the session identifier of a victim
options.D: Log injection, which can forge or hide events and mislead investigations

questions.explanation: Unsanitized input in logs allows forged entries. Encoding or validating log data and protecting log integrity reduces the risk.

questions.question: Inspection of a database shows password values that are 32 hexadecimal characters and identical for users with the same password. What is the likely problem?

options.A: Passwords are stored with a fast, unsalted hash, which makes them easy to crack
options.B: Passwords are stored securely with a slow salted algorithm
options.C: Passwords are encrypted with a strong asymmetric key pair
options.D: Passwords are stored in plain text, which is visible in the values

questions.explanation: Identical hashes for identical passwords show that no salt was used, and a short hexadecimal digest suggests a fast hash. Adaptive, salted hashing is needed.

questions.question: A cloud storage container containing customer documents is readable by anyone with the link. What is the appropriate rating and response?

options.A: A feature that helps customers to retrieve their documents faster
options.B: A finding that concerns only the cloud provider, not the customer
options.C: An unimportant finding, since attackers cannot find links
options.D: A serious misconfiguration: restrict access and review exposure

questions.explanation: Public access to sensitive data is a frequent cause of breaches. Customers are responsible for their configuration, so access should be closed and monitored.

questions.question: Several administrators share one generic administrator account. What is the security problem?

options.A: The account is too secure, since many people know its password
options.B: The account is faster, and so should be recommended for all systems
options.C: Actions cannot be attributed to individuals, and revoking access is harder
options.D: The account causes no problem as long as the password is long

questions.explanation: Shared accounts destroy accountability and complicate offboarding. Individual privileged accounts with logging or privileged access management are preferred.

questions.question: A backup system stores unencrypted copies of production data on a share that is accessible to many staff. What should a tester recommend?

options.A: Encrypt backups, restrict access, and test restoration
options.B: Nothing, since backups are never targeted by attackers
options.C: Delete all backups to avoid the security risk
options.D: Keep backups unencrypted so that they can be restored more quickly

questions.explanation: Backups hold the same sensitive data as production and are attractive targets. They need protection equivalent to the source and must be verified to work.

questions.question: A mobile app should be protected against interception of its traffic by a rogue certificate. Which control should be tested?

options.A: Whether the app uses a large amount of memory in the background
options.B: Whether the app icon looks the same on all supported phones
options.C: Certificate pinning, and that the app refuses untrusted certificates
options.D: Whether the app is downloaded more than a million times per year

questions.explanation: Pinning makes the app accept only expected certificates. Tests with an intercepting proxy show whether the app can be tricked.

questions.question: A web application firewall blocks a simple script injection, but the same payload written with unusual encoding passes. What does this show?

options.A: The firewall is perfect, since it blocked the first attempt
options.B: Encoded payloads cannot be dangerous, since browsers ignore them
options.C: The application is secure because a firewall exists in front of it
options.D: Filtering can be bypassed, so the vulnerability itself must be fixed

questions.explanation: Filters are a compensating control, not a cure. Attackers vary payloads, so input handling and output encoding in the application remain essential.

questions.question: A production application exposes a debug page that lists configuration values and can be reached without login. How should this be classified?

options.A: A significant weakness that discloses configuration information
options.B: A cosmetic issue that can safely be ignored by the team
options.C: A harmless feature that helps operations staff to diagnose issues
options.D: A positive control, since it supports transparency and support work

questions.explanation: Debug functions leak details and often lack protections. They should be disabled or restricted in production, and this is verified during hardening tests.

questions.question: A masked test dataset replaces names with random names but keeps birth dates, postal codes and rare job titles. What is the concern?

options.A: Dates and codes can never identify a person in any context
options.B: The names are too random to be typed by the testers
options.C: Individuals may be re-identified from the remaining attributes
options.D: The data is now useless for any kind of testing

questions.explanation: Quasi-identifiers can single out individuals. Effective masking considers combinations of attributes, not only obvious fields.

questions.question: An account lockout policy locks an account for a full day after three failed logins. What risk should a tester consider besides brute force?

options.A: The policy leaks the source code of the application
options.B: An attacker can lock legitimate users out, creating a denial of service
options.C: The policy makes the passwords weaker than before
options.D: The policy allows unlimited guesses, since the account is locked

questions.explanation: Strict lockouts protect against guessing but can be abused to block users. Balanced designs use delays, throttling or additional verification.

questions.question: A registration form has no protection against automated submission, and thousands of fake accounts are created. Which control should be tested?

options.A: A longer privacy policy on the registration page of the site
options.B: A larger font size for the registration button on all pages
options.C: A different color scheme for the registration form and page
options.D: Bot protection such as rate limiting and challenge mechanisms

questions.explanation: Automated abuse is countered by controls that distinguish humans from scripts and limit request volumes. Tests try to bypass them and check that they work as intended.

questions.question: An organization creates a security champions program in which one developer per team receives extra training. What is the main intended benefit?

options.A: The security team no longer has any role in the organization
options.B: The champions replace all penetration testers
options.C: The champions are responsible for all vulnerabilities from now on
options.D: Security knowledge spreads inside teams and questions get answered locally

questions.explanation: Champions bring security closer to daily work and act as a link to specialists, while responsibility remains shared.

questions.question: Training is given once a year to all staff in a single long session, and behavior does not change. What improvement is most likely to help?

options.A: A longer annual session with more slides
options.B: Testing employees without ever telling them the results
options.C: Removing training altogether, since it does not work
options.D: Short, regular, role-relevant training with practice

questions.explanation: Retention improves with relevance, repetition and practice. One-off, generic sessions rarely change habits.

questions.question: After an incident caused by an employee's mistake, management proposes punishment. What is the likely effect on security?

options.A: People will make fewer mistakes because they fear the consequences
options.B: Reporting will increase because employees want to be honest
options.C: There will be no effect on behavior at all
options.D: People may hide mistakes and avoid reporting, delaying detection

questions.explanation: A blame culture suppresses reporting. A learning approach, focusing on causes and process, improves detection and prevention.

questions.question: Employees reuse the same password on many sites. Which measure best reduces the resulting risk?

options.A: Provide a password manager and require unique passwords plus a second factor
options.B: Require the same password for all sites to make it easier to remember
options.C: Ask employees to write passwords on paper and keep them in their wallets
options.D: Forbid all passwords and rely on usernames alone

questions.explanation: Reuse lets one breach compromise many accounts. Tools that make unique passwords easy, plus a second factor, address the behavior and its consequences.

questions.question: One person can create suppliers, approve invoices and release payments in a finance system. Which principle is violated and what is the risk?

options.A: Separation of duties, which allows undetected fraud
options.B: Defense in depth, which makes the network less redundant
options.C: Confidentiality, which prevents payments being encrypted
options.D: Availability, which makes the system slow for all users

questions.explanation: Dividing critical steps between people creates a check on abuse. Testing roles and permissions shows whether one user can complete a whole fraudulent chain.

questions.question: A team reports that it has tested "all OWASP categories". What additional information makes the claim meaningful?

options.A: Which functions were covered for each category, and how deeply
options.B: The number of testers who wear glasses or contact lenses
options.C: The date on which the categories were first published
options.D: The name of the tool vendor who sponsored the whole test

questions.explanation: Coverage claims need scope and depth. Without them, stakeholders cannot judge what remains untested.

questions.question: Findings in several projects repeatedly involve missing input validation. Which conclusion is most useful for management?

options.A: The root cause is likely in practices such as training or libraries
options.B: The testers are mistaken, so the findings should be ignored
options.C: The issue will disappear by itself without any intervention
options.D: The developers are careless, so they should be replaced soon

questions.explanation: Recurring vulnerability classes point to process or knowledge gaps. Fixing individual defects is necessary, but addressing the cause prevents new ones.

questions.question: A customer asks for the results of a penetration test of a product. Which approach protects the vendor and informs the customer?

options.A: Email the raw scanner output to all of the customers
options.B: Publish the entire report on the public company website
options.C: Refuse to say anything about the testing that took place
options.D: Share a summary under agreement, withholding unfixed weakness details

questions.explanation: Customers need assurance, but details of open vulnerabilities help attackers. Controlled sharing balances transparency and security.

questions.question: Results of this year's test are compared with last year's. Which comparison is most valid?

options.A: Compare like with like: same scope, method and severity scheme
options.B: Compare the raw number of findings, whatever changed in scope
options.C: Compare the length of the reports, since longer reports mean more findings
options.D: Compare the names of the testers

questions.explanation: Trends are meaningful only if the basis is consistent. Differences in scope, depth or ratings must be explained.

questions.question: A risk heat map is proposed for a management presentation of security test results. What should it show?

options.A: Findings positioned by likelihood and impact
options.B: The names of all employees in the organization
options.C: The number of vulnerabilities found per individual tester
options.D: The temperature of the server room during the tests

questions.explanation: A heat map communicates prioritization. It helps decision-makers focus on the highest risks, and should be backed by detailed findings.

questions.question: Which set of key indicators best shows the health of a vulnerability management process?

options.A: The number of pages in the security policy document
options.B: The number of security tools that were purchased this year
options.C: Time to remediate by severity, overdue critical findings, recurrence
options.D: The number of security meetings that were held this year

questions.explanation: These indicators reflect outcomes: how fast serious issues are fixed, what is late and whether problems return. Activity counts do not show risk reduction.
